 obesity. The forms of monogenic obesity known to date can be
classiﬁed into the following 3 categories:
1. Genes involved in the adipocyte-hypothalamic system (leptin/melanocortin axis). The most important genes included in this category are
those coding for leptin (LEP), leptin receptor (LEPR), proopiomelanocortin (POMC), proconvertase 1 (PCSK1), proconvertase 2
(PCSK2), melanocortin receptor 4 (MC4R), and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor g (PPARg). The most common single
gene defect currently identiﬁed in children with obesity is mutations in the melanocortin 4 receptor. The clinical features of
patients affected by these types of monogenic obesities are summarized in Table 1 (Kumar and Kelly, 2017; Martos-Moreno
et al., 2014).
